differences.what: The message narrates that the method was only reached after first reproducing the published white-bear direction and debugging a rendering mismatch, none of which appears in the write-up
differences.message_quote: My first home-built contrasts from self-written prompts all *harmed* the readout. The decisive debug: the server's `prompts`-mode rendering differs from the banks' `chat_dm` rendering (cos 0.55 on identical content), so those directions were computed in the wrong state space. Rebuilding from bank items fixed it.

rationale: The write-up only distinguishes its contrast from "the think/don't-think (white-bear) stance" via a performance comparison (0.73 vs 0.69), without naming the authors or stating the method was derived by first reproducing that published direction. The closing message explicitly names "Raman et al." as authors of "the published method," states it reproduced that method first (0.686 on fit) before building the novel preference-withholding axis, and narrates a debugging story about bank-vs-prompts rendering absent from the write-up — so the message credits and contextualizes the source more fully than the write-up does, while making no false claims about the write-up's own content.
